component.name: Lodestone
component.summary: One library for all your games on Linux

description.p: Lodestone brings the games you own on every store into one library. Epic, GOG, Battle.net, EA and Ubisoft games run through Proton without going through the Steam client; Steam games still use Steam.

ul.li: Steam, Epic Games, GOG, Amazon, Battle.net, EA, Ubisoft, Lutris, Heroic and Minecraft in one place, installed or not
Install, update and uninstall Epic and GOG games directly, and Steam games in the background
Battle.net, EA app and Ubisoft Connect set up on Proton, or used from Lutris or Steam where you already have them
Downloads tab with speed, sizes, time left and history
Play time from Steam, Epic, Lutris and Heroic, plus everything you play through Lodestone
Game details, news, ProtonDB ratings and artwork, with an editor for titles, covers and install locations
MangoHud performance overlay, set up and configured from the app
Steam friends, and who among them owns a game
Mods through Kiln, a separate mod manager: Lodestone shows which games it can mod and plays them with their mods checked
Minecraft hub for mods, resource packs and shaders (in active development: works with ATLauncher today, Prism Launcher support is early)

description.p: Lodestone is not affiliated with Valve, Epic Games, GOG, Amazon, Blizzard, Electronic Arts, Ubisoft or Mojang.

screenshot.caption: Home: recent games, updates, news and play time
Every store in one library, with play time and ProtonDB ratings

description.p: Hotfix: testers can now get test builds of plug-ins.

ul.li: Plug-ins page: a switch, off by default, to also offer test builds (pre-releases) of plug-ins, still checked against GitHub's checksum

description.p: Test release from the comms branch: plug-ins and the Windows build.

ul.li: Plug-ins page: install and update the official plug-ins (Lodestone Beacon, Kiln) from their GitHub releases, checked against GitHub's checksum
Kiln is a plug-in with an on/off switch
The Windows build no longer contains Linux-only code

description.p: The Emulation Update (beta): your ROMs as libraries in Lodestone, with achievements.

ul.li: ROMs in EmuDeck's folder layout show up as one library per system, with ES-DE's game names and covers
Choose the emulator for each system, and install missing emulators from Flathub (and RetroArch cores from libretro) in one click
Emulators installed by Lodestone stay out of your app menu unless you ask for them
RetroAchievements: ROMs are matched by fingerprint, with RetroAchievements names, box art and your achievement progress
Box art from libretro's thumbnail collection for ROMs that have none
Steam achievements in a game's details, with how rare each one is
Lodestone's version is shown in the sidebar and Settings
Steam updates requested from Lodestone start straight away instead of being scheduled for later

description.p: Security and reliability release, following the first full security review (published in the repository).

ul.li: Updated the bundled SQLite (RUSTSEC-2026-0459) and url (RUSTSEC-2026-0592) libraries
Minecraft mod downloads can no longer be written outside the instance folder
The Steam Web API key no longer appears in connection error messages
A strict content security policy for the app window
Sign-in windows only accept the sign-in result from the store's own pages
Downloaded tools are checked against GitHub's published checksums
Steam download progress, speed and folder are shown for downloads Steam started on its own, and a paused Steam download is no longer reported as failed

description.p: Privacy fix: the Epic and GOG sign-in files are now readable only by your own user account, like Lodestone's other stored sign-ins. Lodestone tightens them when it starts and whenever it loads your library.
